question: Does parameter initialization causally bias transformers toward compositional reasoning or direct memorization, and what internal structures accompany the two solutions?

key_findings.claim: Initialization scale selects between an inferential and a symmetric memorizing solution in a controlled two-anchor composition task.
key_findings.evidence: Small initialization generalizes to the held-out reversed anchor pair by composing learned single-anchor functions; larger initialization fits seen pairs symmetrically but fails the withheld direction, while very large scales optimize poorly.

key_findings.claim: The two solutions have different circuits and representation geometry.
key_findings.evidence: Causal/information-flow probes find sequential single-anchor application in the inferential model versus pair-specific combination in the memorizing model; small initialization also produces weight condensation and an ordinal embedding direction.

key_findings.claim: Small initialization plus stronger weight decay improves OOD accuracy on several reasoning benchmarks, but those interventions are partly confounded.
key_findings.evidence: SCAN, COGS, and PrOntoQA experiments favor the small-initialization/high-decay regime; because both settings vary together and results select learning rates across seeds, they do not isolate initialization as the sole cause.

method.core_idea: Vary transformer initialization scale in controlled compositional tasks and connect generalization phases to causal computation paths and weight/embedding structure.
method.mechanism: A synthetic anchor-function dataset withholds one ordered composition while keeping its reverse; phase sweeps, activation interventions, and spectral/geometry probes distinguish algorithmic composition from pair memorization.
assumptions: The withheld ordered pair cleanly separates composition from memorization.
Initialization scale is not overwhelmed by optimizer and normalization dynamics.
Mechanisms in small controlled transformers transfer to natural-language reasoning tasks.

techniques.role: Creates an exact train-test distinction between inference and pair memorization.
Maps optimization regimes over scale and learning rate.
Tests whether learned layers apply component functions sequentially.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic two-anchor composition with one direction withheld
evaluations.metric: Training and OOD accuracy across initialization and learning rate
evaluations.result: Small-scale models infer the held-out composition; intermediate scales memorize seen ordered pairs; very large scales often fail to fit.
evaluations.baseline: Alternative initialization scales under matched architectures

evaluations.result: The reasoning-versus-memorization transition persists in the tested GPT-2 configuration.
Small initialization with stronger weight decay generally improves reported OOD performance; more PrOntoQA data can move larger-initialized models toward reasoning.

limitations: Most mechanistic evidence comes from a deliberately small synthetic task.
Natural-task experiments co-vary initialization and weight decay, weakening causal attribution.
Best-of-nine learning-rate selection over few seeds may overstate regime robustness.
failure_modes: Extremely small initialization can slow optimization or become sensitive to normalization details.
A model can fit every observed ordered pair while learning no reusable composition rule.
The apparent reasoning circuit may change with architecture, data diversity, or scale.
reusable_insights: Training hyperparameters can select qualitatively different algorithms at identical train loss.
A compositional benchmark should withhold directed combinations, not merely random examples.
Mechanistic claims are stronger when causal path tests agree with representation geometry and OOD behavior.
open_questions: Can initialization and weight decay be disentangled factorially on larger reasoning benchmarks?
Which early-training statistics predict the eventual reasoning basin before OOD labels are consulted?
Do the same phase transitions occur in pretrained billion-parameter models during fine-tuning?

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
competitive_landscape.difference: Grokking emphasizes delayed generalization under extended training; this work varies initialization to select different solutions and analyzes their computation paths.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Understanding Grokking: An Effective Theory of Representation Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: The effective-theory paper maps data and regularization phases; this paper foregrounds initialization scale and directed function composition in transformers.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokked Transformers are Implicit Reasoners: A Mechanistic Journey to the Edge of Generalization
competitive_landscape.difference: That work studies rule-based implicit reasoning acquired through grokking; this paper contrasts initialization-selected compositional and symmetric-memorization circuits without requiring the same delayed-training trajectory.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: grokking phase diagrams and mechanistic studies predate this paper. Its specific contribution is evidence that initialization scale selects between two identifiable transformer algorithms on directed composition, with preliminary transfer to SCAN, COGS, and PrOntoQA.
reviewer_notes: Full text, synthetic setup, phase sweeps, circuit analysis, natural-task experiments, and stated limitations were checked. Competitor primary sources checked 2026-08-23. Natural-task causal attribution is lower confidence because initialization and regularization co-vary.
